text:
olivia: Quick follow-up on the rollout metadata RFC — I think we need a compact way to express cross-version compatibility rules and soft-deprecation windows. current idea: add a `compatibility_matrix_id` reference plus optional inline `compat_hints` to avoid per-request bloat. thoughts?

sam: I like the id+hints pattern. big win: keep per-request headers tiny. downside: more indirection when debugging. can we make the id resolvable via our control plane and cacheable in clients? :thinking:

maria: Observability note: if we add indirection we need strong telemetry hooks. suggest schema fields for `signal_version` and `metadata_source` so we can correlate client behavior with the active compat doc. otherwise tying regressions back will be a pain.

dinesh: runtime constraints: parsing an arbitrary compat JSON per request is a no-go. runtime should only receive compact tokens/ids. please avoid adding lots of inline rules that force the token path to grow. we can fetch heavyweight docs asynchronously and populate local resolvers.

kevin: from SRE/rollouts: how would this interact with canarying and automatic fallback? we need to map compat rules to rollout cohorts. otherwise we risk serving a model that is incompatible with client expectations during canary.

olivia: good call. sketching a minimal contract: `rollout_metadata` = { "ref": "compat-<id>", "hints": "short base64 or compressed blob (optional)", "canary_cohort_hint": "stable|canary|all" } — runtime only sees `ref` + `cohort` at call time. full doc lives in control plane and in object storage.

sam: also: proto vs JSON for the stored doc? proto gains size+parsing speed but makes ad-hoc inspection harder. maybe JSON in storage + gzipped blobs for transport and a small binary proto for runtime caches.

maria: +1 to explicit schema versioning. add `schema_version` in the control-plane doc. we can then emit telemetry when clients read mismatched schema vs runtime support. helps rolling upgrades.

dinesh: runtime support: please constrain the runtime-visible contract to these primitives: `ref_id`, `fallback_order[]`, `deprecation_deadline` (iso8601), and a tiny `flags` bitfield. all other richness stays off-path.

olivia: example control-plane doc idea (human readable):
```json
{
  "schema_version": "2026-03-1",
  "ref_id": "compat-2026-03-001",
  "fallback_order": ["v2.3","v2.2","v1.9"],
  "deprecation_deadline": "2026-05-01T00:00:00Z",
  "migration_notes": "clients should stop expecting X-legacy-field by 2026-05",
  "signals": { "expected_prefix_shifts": true }
}
```

sam: small perf thought: make `ref_id` stable and TTL-ed in SDK caches. when control plane updates ref -> new id. avoids invalidating caches mid-rollout.

kevin: ops checklist item: we need a migration playbook that ties `ref_id` changes to canary windows, alert thresholds (error spike + misparse rate), and auto-fallback triggers. can we add optional `rollback_on_error: true|false` flag into the doc?

olivia: yes, propose a `safety_policy` block with `rollback_on_error`, `error_rate_threshold`, and `min_canary_requests`. runtime only reads the small policy subset.

maria: testing: we should add a synthetic eval where clients with older schema intentionally receive a compat-ref that omits a field to validate fallback behavior. schedule this with QA prior to any control-plane migration.

dinesh: implementation note: runtime will expose a small probe endpoint that returns the active `ref_id` and resolved fallback for a tenant. that'll make debugging easier and avoid full doc fetches.

rollout-bot: :robot_face: Canary job started for `compat-2026-03-001` (cohort: canary). 5% traffic routed.

olivia: next steps: (1) i'll draft a short PR defining the control-plane document schema + `safety_policy` subset for runtime, (2) @sam will prototype the id cache TTL + proto serialization, (3) @maria to write the telemetry contract, (4) @dinesh to mock the runtime probe endpoint. i'll link an initial draft by EOD tomorrow. thanks all :thumbsup:

sam: lgtm. i'll aim for a 48h prototype.

maria: adding QA tests to backlog.

dinesh: will stub probe today.

kevin: i'll draft the ops runbook checklist and alert thresholds.
